decisions.latin: annuntiábo veritátem tuam in ore meo
decisions.why: *in ore meo* (ἐν τῷ στόματί μου) is instrumental: 'with my mouth' (DRB). *na minha boca* keeps the Latin's preposition, but in Portuguese it places the truth inside the mouth rather than saying it aloud. 88:2–2b is also the Introit/antiphon text *Misericórdias Dómini in ætérnum cantábo: in generatiónem et generatiónem annuntiábo veritátem tuam in ore meo* (missa Sancti 07-01, grep), so the colon is also sung on its own.

options.label: com a minha boca
options.note: Ruling: the instrumental sense, DRB 'with my mouth'.

decisions.latin: præparábitur véritas tua … præparábo semen tuum … præparátio sedis tuæ
decisions.why: The psalm uses *præparáre* three times, all built on ἑτοιμάζω, which also means 'establish, make ready' (Hebrew *kûn*, 'set firm'). MS1932 turns each one into a different word (*solidamente estabelecida*, *conservarei*, *a base*). Keeping *preparar* all three times lets the Latin's repetition be heard (rule 6), and every use is still intelligible: a truth made ready in the heavens, a descendance made ready, and justice and judgement as what makes the throne ready. *Preparar* is also this psalter's word for the verb (22:5, 64:7, 67:11). The cost is that *preparar a tua descendência* is thinner in Portuguese than 'establish'.

options.label: preparar ×3
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's one word, kept three times.

options.label: firmar ×2, base
options.note: The Hebrew sense of *kûn*, which the Greek also allows. It collides with *Firmei aliança* (88:4) and *Firme-se* (88:14).

options.label: MS1932
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: three words for one.

decisions.latin: Dispósui testaméntum
decisions.why: *dispónere testaméntum* (διεθέμην διαθήκην) means to make a covenant. The glossary's *testaméntum* row gives *firmar aliança* for *dispónere/ordináre testaméntum*, and 82:6 reads *firmaram aliança*. *Fazer aliança* (MS1932) is the plainer everyday idiom.

options.label: Dispus a aliança
options.note: The Latin's own verb; heard as 'arranged'.

decisions.latin: Confitebúntur cæli mirabília tua … étenim veritátem tuam
decisions.why: D5 settles *confitéri* (to God) as *dar graças a*, but here the verb takes an accusative of the thing praised (*mirabília tua*, and *veritátem tuam* in the second colon). The precedent is 70:22, where *confitébor tibi … veritátem tuam* became *vos darei graças pela vossa verdade*: the thing is taken with *por*, and the second colon carries *por* over. *Celebrar* would keep the transitive build but gives up D5's verb. The Latinist (minor) asked for *celebrarão* (the accusative kept) and *deveras* for *étenim*. Refused: D5 is settled and 70:22 already has *dar graças por* with an accusative. *e também* renders *étenim* (καί). *Celebrarão* stays option 1.

options.label: celebrarão
options.note: Keeps the accusative; loses D5's verb.

decisions.latin: tuum brácchium cum poténtia
decisions.why: The colon has no verb. The Greek σὸς ὁ βραχίων μετὰ δυναστείας makes *tuum* the predicate ('yours is the arm, with might'), and that continues 88:12's *Tui sunt cæli, et tua est terra*. So the draft reads *vosso é o braço*, which echoes *Vossos são os céus*. *O vosso braço está com potência* reads *tuum* as a plain possessive. *Poténtia* → *potência* follows the glossary row (64:7, 79:3). The Latinist (minor) asked for the verbless *o vosso braço com potência*. This is refused because the Greek fixes the predicate reading and the echo of 88:12 is the Latin's own (*Tui … tua … tuum*); his form is kept as an option. The stylist's *poderio* was refused because *poténtia → potência* is the row (64:7, 70:16, 79:3).

options.label: vosso é o braço com potência

forms.b13: vosso é o braço com potência

options.note: Ruling: the Greek's predicate, the echo of 88:12.

options.label: o vosso braço está com potência

forms.b13: o vosso braço está com potência

options.note: *tuum* as a plain possessive, with a copula supplied.

options.label: cheio de potência (MS1932)

forms.b13: o vosso braço está cheio de potência

options.note: MS1932's *está cheio de poder*, with the row's noun.

options.label: o vosso braço com potência
options.note: The Latinist: verbless, as the Latin.

decisions.latin: in beneplácito tuo
decisions.why: *Beneplácitum* as a noun (εὐδοκία, good pleasure) has no settled row. Draft 1 had *no vosso beneplácito*; the stylist called it chancery Latin and the blind reader listed it as unknown. *Boa vontade* is already the word for *bona volúntas* (5:13b, 50:20), so it is not free. *Favor* is plain and keeps the sense of goodwill freely given.

options.label: no vosso favor
options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist's word, with the Latin's *in*.

options.label: no vosso beneplácito
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin's word; unknown to the blind reader.

decisions.latin: Dómini est assúmptio nostra
decisions.why: *Assúmptio* renders ἀντίλημψις, 'support, protection', which shares its root with 88:27's ἀντιλήμπτωρ (Latin *suscéptor*). D19 and the glossary give *suscéptor* the word *amparo*, so *o nosso amparo* keeps the Greek link between the two verses. DRB has 'our protection'. MS1932 (*o Senhor tomou-nos por seus*) reads the word as 'taking up', which is the Latin's surface sense. The cost: 88:27 *suscéptor* is also *amparo*, so two Latin words share one Portuguese word, but they are the same word in the Greek. The Latinist (minor) asked for *acolhimento*, to keep 88:19 and 88:27 apart. Refused for the Greek link (D15's test); it remains option 3.

options.label: o nosso acolhimento
options.note: Close to the Latin's surface (*assúmere*, taking up).

decisions.latin: concídam a fácie ipsíus inimícos ejus
decisions.why: *concídere* means 'to cut down, cut to pieces' (L&S); συγκόψω means 'to strike down'. *Destroçar* keeps the violence of cutting to pieces. *Abater* is the glossary's word for *depónere* (people). *a fácie ipsíus* becomes *diante dele*, as the *a fácie* row does where 'from the face of' is not Portuguese (37:4, 60:4).

decisions.latin: Pater meus es tu
decisions.why: D17 (address follows the speaker) names 88:27–28. The whole oracle 88:20–37 is God's speech, and in it the Anointed's cry to the Father is quoted. The line mirrors 2:7 *Fílius meus es tu* → *Tu és meu Filho*, the other side of the same relation, so *tu* makes the pair answer each other. *Vós* (D1) is the voice of the one praying, and this line is spoken inside God's own words. The Christmas versicle *V. Ipse invocábit me. R. Pater meus es tu* (horas Sancti 12-25, grep) puts it in the choir's mouth; there *vós* would be defensible, which is why it stays an option. MS1932 has *Tu és meu Pai*.

decisions.latin: Et ponam in sǽculum sǽculi semen ejus
decisions.why: *Ponam* is the third *pónere* in five verses (88:26 *ponam in mari*, 88:28 *primogénitum ponam*, 88:30). *Porei* keeps the Latin's verb and its sense of setting in place, which the ear follows after 88:26's *porei*. *Estabelecerei* reads more smoothly but belongs to *constitúere* (row; 88:48). DRB's 'make … to endure' adds a verb.

options.label: farei durar
options.note: DRB 'make to endure'; MS1932 *farei que … subsista*.

decisions.latin: Si justítias meas profanáverint
decisions.why: The plural *justítiæ* renders δικαιώματα, 'ordinances'. The open glossary row gives *as justiças* and says it 'may want *preceitos*' where the Greek is δικαιώματα, which is the case here. Beside *lex*, *judícia* and *mandáta* (88:31–32), a word for statutes is clearly meant. *As minhas justiças* keeps the Latin's word. It also keeps this psalm's other *justítia* (88:14, 88:16) audible, but a Brazilian ear hears it as abstract. DRB has 'my justices'. The ruling keeps the row's word until the row is settled, and offers *preceitos* as the option.

options.label: as minhas justiças
options.note: Ruling: the row (open) and the Latin's word.

decisions.latin: in verbéribus
decisions.why: *verbera* means blows or lashes (μάστιξιν). D39 gives *flagelo* to *plaga/flagéllum*. *Açoites* (MS1932, DRB 'stripes') keeps *verbera* distinct from those words.

decisions.latin: Misericórdiam autem meam non dispérgam ab eo: neque nocébo in veritáte mea
decisions.why: *Dispérgere* (διασκεδάσω, 'scatter, break up') has *dispersar* in 88:11, but *dispersar a misericórdia dele* is not Portuguese, so the draft reads *retirar* (MS1932), which yields to the ear. The second colon, *nocébo in veritáte mea* (ἀδικήσω, 'deal wrongly'), keeps *nocére → fazer mal* from 88:23, so the oracle's two *nocére* answer each other: the enemy will not harm David, and God will not do harm against his own truth. It is obscure in Portuguese. MS1932's *nem lhe faltarei à verdade* gives the sense. Draft 2 (the Latinist): *dissiparei*, which keeps the scattering and still reads as Portuguese. The blind reader found *nem farei mal na minha verdade* obscure; kept, for the Latin's echo of 88:23 (no Latinist remark), with MS1932's sense as the option.

options.label: dissiparei / farei mal
options.note: Ruling (v2): the Latinist's *dissipar*, which keeps the image of scattering and is Portuguese with *misericórdia*.

options.label: retirarei / farei mal
options.note: Draft 1: *retirar* (MS1932), the ear for *dispérgere*; the Latinist found the image lost.

options.label: dispersarei para longe
options.note: The Latin's verb kept, with a supplied *para longe*.

options.label: faltarei à minha verdade
options.note: MS1932's sense ('nor will I fail my truth', DRB).

decisions.latin: Semel jurávi in sancto meo: Si David méntiar
decisions.why: *Si … méntiar* is the Hebrew oath formula ('if I lie' = 'I will surely not lie'). Portuguese has no such idiom, and *Se eu mentir a Davi: a sua descendência permanecerá* reads as a condition with the opposite sense, so the formula yields to grammar (D2): *não mentirei a Davi* (DRB, MS1932). *In sancto meo* (ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ μου; the Hebrew is 'by my holiness') is the thing sworn by. *Pela minha santidade* (MS1932, DRB 'by my holiness') gives the sense. *No meu santo* is 59:8's wording for *in sancto suo* (with *falou*), but after *jurei* it names no oath. The responsory in Commune C2 (grep) reads *Semel jurávi in sancto meo: Semen ejus in ætérnum manébit*, omitting *Si David méntiar*, so each half must stand alone. Both do. The Latinist (minor) asked for the formula to be kept (*se eu mentir a Davi!*). Refused: the blind reader would hear a condition that says the opposite. His form is option 2 (*pela minha santidade: se eu mentir*).

options.label: pela minha santidade: não mentirei
options.note: Ruling: the sense of both idioms.

options.label: no meu santo: se eu mentir
options.note: Both kept literally (59:8's *no seu santo*); the oath is left for the reader to recognize.

options.label: pela minha santidade: se eu mentir
options.note: Only the oath formula kept literally.

decisions.latin: distulísti Christum tuum
decisions.why: The glossary gives *différre → adiar* (77:21 *ouviu, e adiou*). ἀνεβάλου means 'you put off, deferred', and the Hebrew means 'you were enraged with' (which DRB follows here, against its own Latin). The Latin says 'put off': the Anointed's day is postponed. *Christus → Cristo* (D19; *o vosso Cristo*, as 83:10). MS1932 *repeliste* would merge with *repulísti* in the same verse.

options.label: retardastes
options.note: 'Held back'; the Greek's sense, more concrete.

decisions.latin: Evertísti testaméntum … profanásti in terra Sanctuárium ejus
decisions.why: *evértere* means 'to overturn' (κατέστρεψας). *Derrubar* keeps the image of a covenant thrown down like a building. *Anular* (MS1932) gives the legal sense and drops the image. *in terra* is εἰς τὴν γῆν, '(down) to the ground': *profanastes por terra* says it, while *na terra* (DRB 'on the earth') keeps the Latin's ambiguity.

options.label: Derrubastes / por terra
options.note: Ruling: the image; the Greek's sense of *in terra*.

decisions.latin: Destruxísti omnes sepes ejus: posuísti firmaméntum ejus formídinem
decisions.why: *sepes* means hedges or fences (φραγμούς). 79:13 used *cerca* for *macéria*, so *sebes* keeps the two Latin words apart. *Firmaméntum* here is neither God nor the sky: D31 leaves it to the verse. Its Greek is ὀχυρώματα, 'strongholds', and *fortaleza* holds both 'stronghold' and 'firmness'. *Pónere* + predicate follows its row (*fazer de*, 17:12). *formído → pavor* (54:5). Draft 2: *cercas*: the blind reader listed *sebes* as unknown, and a word nobody knows is a higher cost than sharing *cerca* with 79:13.

options.label: cercas / fortaleza

forms.f41: fizestes da sua fortaleza um pavor

options.note: Ruling (v2): *cercas*, since the blind reader did not know *sebes*; it shares 79:13's word for *macéria*.

forms.f41: fizestes da sua fortaleza um pavor
fizestes da sua firmeza um pavor
pusestes o pavor nas suas fortalezas

decisions.latin: Avertísti adjutórium … Úsquequo, Dómine, avértis in finem
decisions.why: *Avértere* occurs twice. 88:47 has no object, as 84:4 *avertísti ab ira*, which was ruled reflexive *afastastes-vos* with *afastar* for the whole of Ps 84. The draft follows that psalm: *Afastastes o auxílio*, and *vos afastais*. 88:47 is D27's formula *Até quando, Senhor, … para sempre?* (78:5). *Exardéscere → inflamar-se* as 38:4.

decisions.latin: Destruxísti eum ab emundatióne
decisions.why: The Greek is κατέλυσας ἀπὸ καθαρισμοῦ αὐτόν, 'you made him cease from (his) cleansing'. DRB reads 'thou hast made his purification to cease'. Portuguese cannot say *destruir de*. *Destruístes-lhe a purificação* keeps *destruir* (the row names 88:45), *eum* as the one it happens to, and *purificação*. It loses only the preposition, and it fits the Latin's length. *emundátio* follows the *mundáre/emundáre* row (*purificar*). Draft 2: the Latinist showed that draft 1 made the purification the object; *apartando-o da* restores both *eum* and *ab* at the cost of about two syllables.

options.label: Vós o destruístes, apartando-o

forms.em45: Vós o destruístes, apartando-o da purificação

options.note: Ruling (v2): the Latinist's reading — *eum* the object, *ab* as separation — with proclisis (*Destruístes-o* is not the *vós* form).

options.label: Destruístes-lhe a purificação (draft 1)
options.note: Draft 1: purification made the thing destroyed (Latinist, minor); the stylist found *-lhe* stiff.

options.label: Destruístes a sua purificação
options.note: The stylist's plain form; the same reading as draft 1.

options.label: privando-o da purificação

forms.em45: Vós o destruístes, privando-o da purificação

options.note: Keeps *eum* as the object and the *ab*; four syllables long.

decisions.latin: perfudísti eum confusióne
decisions.why: *perfúndere* means to pour over or drench (κατέχεας αὐτοῦ αἰσχύνην, 'you poured shame on him'). *Banhar* keeps the liquid image. *Cobrir* (MS1932) is the usual Portuguese build, and it is the word already given to *operíre* (70:13) and *cooperíre* (43:16, 68:8). *Confúsio → vergonha*, as 70:13 and 43:16.

decisions.latin: numquid enim vane constituísti omnes fílios hóminum?
decisions.why: The glossary gives *constitúere → estabelecer*. The Greek has ἔκτισας ('created'), and MS1932 has *criaste*, but the Latin chose another verb than 88:13's *creásti*. *Estabelecestes em vão* is a little stiff. The row is followed and *fizestes* offered.

decisions.latin: quod contínui in sinu meo multárum géntium
decisions.why: The Greek is ὑπέσχον, 'I held up under, bore'. The Hebrew means 'I carry in my bosom'. The glossary gives *continére → conter* (76:10), and *conter no meu seio* here means holding the reproach in, not restraining it. *Guardei* (DO; MS1932 *conservo*) and *carreguei* (the Hebrew and Greek image) are the options. *multárum géntium* depends on *oppróbrii*: the reproach of many nations. Draft 2 moves *de muitas nações* forward, next to *que* (the stylist): at the end it dangled, and the blind reader lost the parse. The genitive still belongs to the reproach.

options.label: guardei
options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist and the blind reader both heard *contive* as 'I restrained'.

options.label: contive
options.note: Draft 1: the row (76:10); heard in Brazil as 'restrained'.

decisions.latin: exprobravérunt commutatiónem Christi tui
decisions.why: *Commutátio* is settled as *troca* (D43, 43:13), but the row says 88:52 'will want its own look'. The Greek ἀντάλλαγμα means 'exchange, what is given in exchange'. DRB reads 'the change of thy anointed', MS1932 *mudança*, and 54:20b already took the local sense *mudança*. Here *a mudança do vosso Cristo* is the reversal of the Anointed's fortune, the theme of 88:39–46. *A troca* is kept as the option.

choices.88:2: *in ætérnum → para sempre* (D23). Read alone as the Introit/antiphon incipit.
choices.88:3: *Quóniam dixísti:* introduces God's words, which run on in the first person in 88:4–5 (as the Latin punctuates). *ædificáre → edificar* (77:69).
choices.88:4: God to David: *tu* (D17). *Usque in ætérnum → para todo o sempre* (D37). *semen → descendência* (D32). *eléctus → escolhido* (77:31).
choices.88:5: *sedes → trono* (row). *In generatiónem et generatiónem → de geração em geração* (formula).
choices.88:7: The Latin has no second *quis* in the second colon; the question runs on from the first, and the draft keeps that (no *e quem*). *æquábitur → se igualará*. Draft 2: *Quóniam → Pois* here (the stylist: *Porque quem* stutters /ke ke/ at the opening, and the blind reader heard *Porque* as 'because', not as a question).
choices.88:8: *consílium sanctórum → conselho dos santos* (D33: a deliberating body). *terríbilis → terrível*; *in circúitu → ao redor* (row names 88:9).
choices.88:10: The emphatic *tu … tu* (88:10–12) kept as *vós* every time. *mitigáre → abrandar* (84:4). *potéstas maris → o poder do mar*: *poder* is *virtus*'s word in this psalter too (88:9, 11, 18); DRB 'the power of the sea' has the same pair. Option *o domínio do mar*.
choices.88:11: *dispérgere → dispersar* (row, 88:11 named). Natural order *o soberbo como a um ferido*.
choices.88:12: *orbis terræ → o mundo* (D30); *plenitúdo → plenitude*; *aquilo → norte* (D43). The resumptive *vós os fundastes … vós os criastes* supplies the object that the Latin's fronted accusatives carry. Rhyme *fundastes … criastes* accepted (checks): it is the Latin's own parallel *tu fundásti … tu creásti*.
choices.88:14: *Firmétur … exaltétur* as reflexive jussives (*Firme-se … exalte-se*); *firmáre → firmar* (row). *déxtera → direita* (row). Articles supplied to *justiça e juízo*.
choices.88:15: *præcédent fáciem tuam → irão diante da vossa face*. *scire → conhecer* (row, open); *jubilátio → aclamação* (D43 names 88:15).
choices.88:16: *tota die → o dia todo* (D24). The first colon carries two clauses, as in the Latin.
choices.88:18: *eórum → deles*, so that *seu* is not heard as God's. *cornu → chifre* (row). The blind reader flagged *chifre* for the Brazilian slang sense; the row (open) keeps the image, as 88:25.
choices.88:20: *sanctis tuis* (ὁσίοις) → *aos vossos santos* (row). *adjutórium → auxílio*; *in poténte → num poderoso* (the responsory in Commune C4 reads *super poténtem*; *num* follows the psalter's *in*). *plebs → povo*.
choices.88:21: Read alone as a gradual/responsory (Commune C4, missa Sancti, grep). *óleum sanctum meum → o meu óleo santo* (adjective after, as *monte santo*).
choices.88:22: *auxiliári → ajudar* here and in 88:44, so that 88:44's *adjutórium* (*auxílio*) and *auxiliátus* stay distinct as they are in the Latin. *confortáre → fortalecer*.
choices.88:23: *non appónet nocére → não voltará a fazer-lhe mal* (the *appónere ut* row). The responsory's variant *non nocébit ei* would be *não lhe fará mal*.
choices.88:29: *serváre* with a dative of person → *conservar* (the *serváre* row lists 88:29; *guardar* is kept for *custodíre*, 88:32). *fidélis → fiel*; the copula *será* supplied.
choices.88:35: *írrita fácere → tornar vão*; the resumptive *o* supplied after the fronted object.
choices.88:37: *in conspéctu meo → à minha vista* (22:5, 55:9). The copula *será* supplied in the first colon. *testis in cælo fidélis → e testemunha fiel no céu*: the Latin leaves open whether the moon is the witness or another; the draft does not decide (MS1932 adds *(Deus)*).
choices.88:39: *repéllere → repelir* (D42 names 88:39); *despícere → desdenhar* (row, 21:25). The Latin gives both verbs no object; kept.
choices.88:42: *diripere → saquear* (D43 names 88:42). *transeúntes viam → os que passam pelo caminho* (79:13). *oppróbrium → afronta* (78:4, 43:14).
choices.88:43: *depriméntium → dos que o oprimem*: *deprímere* is 'press down'. *oprimir* is its nearest plain verb; *rebaixam* is an option not taken because it is weaker. *lætificáre → alegrar* (row).
choices.88:45: *collídere → esmagar* (row, passive, open); *in terram → por terra* (motion).
choices.88:46: *minoráre → abreviar* (MS1932): 'make smaller' of days. *diminuir* is the *diminúere* row's.
choices.88:47: D27's formula; *in finem → para sempre*. *exardéscere → inflamar-se* (38:4).
choices.88:48: *Memoráre → Lembrai-vos* (safe: enclitic, D13). *substántia mea → o meu ser* (D39). Draft 2 (the stylist): *do que é* for *quæ* (draft 1 *de qual é* sounded translated), and *em vão* before the verb, which is the Latin's order (*vane constituísti*).
choices.88:49: The Latin has no relative before *éruet*; *que* supplied (grammar, D2) so that the second colon is heard as the same man. *éruere … de manu → arrancar … da mão* (85:13). *ínferi → inferno* (row).
choices.88:52: *Quod exprobravérunt* → *Com que afrontaram*: *quod* resumes *oppróbrii* (51), an internal accusative ('the reproach with which they reproached'). *exprobráre → afrontar* (row).
choices.88:53: *Benedíctus Dóminus → Bendito o Senhor* (row); *fiat, fiat → assim seja, assim seja* (D41 names 88:53).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps088.md (no Diurnal: not a day-hour psalm) and the glossary rows. Hard readings: 88:13 *tuum brácchium cum poténtia* with no verb; 88:19 *assúmptio* (tied to 88:27 through the Greek); 88:27 the address inside God's speech (D17); 88:34 *dispérgere* and *nocére in veritáte*; 88:36 the oath formula *Si … méntiar*; 88:39 *distulísti*; 88:41 *sepes* and *firmaméntum*; 88:45 *ab emundatióne*; 88:51 *contínui in sinu*; 88:52 *commutátio*. Liturgical colons that are read alone (DO, grep): 88:2–2b (Introit/antiphon), 88:21–23 (gradual, responsories in Commune C4), 88:20a (responsory, *super poténtem*), 88:27 (Christmas versicle), 88:36–38 (responsory in Commune C2).

Hard pass. Soft flags accepted: 88:2b and 88:5 −6 (the formula *de geração em geração* is shorter than the Latin's); 88:4b +4 (*para todo o sempre*, D37); 88:9b +3 and 88:25a +4 (copula *está / estarão* and articles supplied); 88:15 +3/+4 (*irão diante da*, *bem-aventurado*); 88:16a −3; 88:22a −4 (*ajudará* is shorter than *auxiliábitur*); 88:30a +5 (*pelos séculos dos séculos*, the formula); 88:31b −4, 88:35b −4, 88:44b −3, 88:51a −3 (the Portuguese is complete); 88:36 +4/+5 (the oath made explicit, *permanecerá*); 88:42b +3; 88:47a +3 (D27 formula); 88:53b +4 (D41 *assim seja*); 88:12 rhyme (the Latin's parallel).

audit.note: claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, blind. 66 readings and 7 unknown words. Acted on: 88:7 (question not heard, *Pois*), 88:18 *beneplácito* unknown (*favor*), 88:41 *sebes* unknown (*cercas*), 88:51 parse lost (order and *guardei*). The rest are accepted: the Latin's own obscurities (88:34b, 88:37 the witness, 88:45 purification, 88:52 *mudança*), settled words (*Cristo* D19, *poderes* D43, *para sempre* in D27's formula, *voltará a* in the *appónere* row), and *chifre* (row, open; the image stays, rule 5). *Tabor*, *Hermon*, *profanastes*, *açoites* stay as they are: they are proper names and words that belong to the register.
